posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
I would prefer some kind of illustrated overview of the events of Sentinels Comics rather than the actual issues themselves.  GtG's strengths seem to be in plotting out interesting stories and characters but maybe not so much in telling the line-by-line details of those stories.  For example, pg. 5 of FF Annual #1 has Legacy confronting Baron Blade with this awesome dialog:

"I should have known it was you when I received reports of disturbances in the airspace over the center of the Atlantic Ocean.  Though you should know that, no matter what terrible plot you are enacting, I will stop you."

To which Baron Blade replies:

"You seem so certain! As always, you are the greatest obstacle!  Not the limitations of the materials, nor the energy consumption of my inventions, but you, a mere man!"

That kind of stilted dialog is fine when you're describing an encounter between archetypes, but as soon as you imagine those words actually coming out of someone's mouth, you cringe a little.  No offense meant, but I know I couldn't read dozens of comics like that.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
As someone who started reading superhero comics in the 00s (always loved superhero A/V media, but never got into the comics before then), I gotta admit that reading anything written before the mid-90s or so could sometimes be really painful to read.

I don't mind SotM because it's deliberately designed as an homage to comics of all eras so I enjoy it as that sort of sometimes intentionally cheesy pastiche, but the actual RL comics just don't age very well.

Hence why I said I'd be pretty happy to get Tactics-style vignettes on a semi-regular basis; I think they're at a great place quality-wise while still having just the right amount of cheese and humor going on.
